On 30 August 1999, in a vote run by the United Nations, 78.5 percent of East Timorese chose independence over autonomy within Indonesia. Nearly all voters turned out.

The vote became possible after the fall of Suharto, when President Habibie offered it. Militias backed by the Indonesian army then killed about 1,400 people, burned most buildings and drove hundreds of thousands into West Timor.

An international force led by Australia landed on 20 September and ended the violence. The United Nations governed the territory until independence in 2002 under Xanana Gusmão. See also Santa Cruz massacre.
